// @path: src/lib/ops/reads.ts
// @expect: OPS-IMPORT-ALLOWLIST
// The bare side-effect import, `import "x"` with no binding, of something that
// is not on the ops allowlist.
//
// This fixture exists because of what the scanner had to be narrowed to on
// 2026-08-24. The bare-import pattern used to be anchored to a word boundary
// alone, which made the word `import` at the tail of ANY string literal look
// like an import statement (see good-string-literal-ending-in-import.txt). It is
// now anchored to a statement position instead — start of line, or after `;`,
// `{` or `}`.
//
// DO NOT DELETE THIS AS REDUNDANT WITH THE OTHER FIFTY-EIGHT.
//
// Fifty-eight fixtures in this corpus already contain `import "server-only";`,
// so the bare form is exercised constantly and this one looks like more of the
// same. It is not. `server-only` is on the allowlist, so all fifty-eight pass
// whether the scanner reads their bare import or not — remove the pattern
// entirely and every one of them still goes green.
//
// A canary that cannot fail is not a canary. This is the only fixture in the
// corpus where a bare import must be REFUSED, so it is the only one that would
// notice if the bare-import pattern were narrowed too far, mistyped, or dropped.
// Deleting it takes the coverage with it and leaves fifty-eight files that look
// like coverage and are not.
//
// A side-effect import is worth catching in its own right. It runs a module for
// what it does on load rather than for anything it returns, which is precisely
// the shape that reads as harmless in review.
import "@/lib/mailer";

export async function nothingToSeeHere() {
  return true;
}
